title: Introduce simulated-prompt playground and lightweight telemetry shims for local RAG development
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Added a local RAG playground that generates synthetic prompts and a set of opt-in telemetry shims for dev environments. No runtime changes to production SDKs. Useful for testing prompt sets, latency profiling and end-to-end instrumentation in local workflows.
description: Motivation: iterating on RAG prompts and tool-calling flows is slow when you need to coordinate a corpus, instrument telemetry, and run the full stack. This PR introduces a lightweight 'simulated-prompt' playground that lets developers generate synthetic user conversations and instrument per-step telemetry without needing a full backend dataset or production tracing. Changes include: 1) a new examples/simplay directory with a small CLI and a browser sandbox to create, replay, and mutate synthetic prompts and retrieval traces; 2) opt-in telemetry shims that emit structured probe events to console, file, or a dev-collector endpoint so teams can prototype tracing and quality signals locally; 3) docs and quickstart: a markdown quickstart that explains common workflows (fuzzing prompt variants, tracing tool calls, and running regressions with seed sets); 4) a few small helpers for mocking embeddings and retrieval layers so the playground can run offline. Usage: yarn workspace @redwood/examples simplay:dev starts the local sandbox; simplay:cli run --seed 42 --scenario tool_calling will produce a replay.json and telemetry.log. The telemetry shims are behind a FEATURE_SIMPLAY_TELEMETRY env var and default to disabled. Security: all synthetic data stays local by default; the dev-collector supports TLS and API key config for teams who want to forward events to a staging telemetry cluster. Testing: added unit tests for the synthetic prompt generator and an integration smoke test for the CLI. See commits and files changed for details. Checklist: - [x] Add playground code and mocks - [x] Add telemetry shims and docs - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Add quickstart doc and example seed sets

chore(simplay): add mocks for embeddings and retrieval
test(simplay): unit tests for generator and CLI
review_comments: Tom Hsu: Nice dev DX improvement overall. Two requests: (1) can we make the default log path configurable via CLI flag in addition to env var? (2) please add a small section in the quickstart describing how to opt out of forwarding events to remote collectors.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Thanks Tom — added --log-path to the CLI and expanded the quickstart to show the FEATURE_SIMPLAY_TELEMETRY toggle and collector opt-out. Updated the docs in the latest commit.
Liam O'Connor: The generator seeds look nondeterministic in one branch of the code; please ensure deterministic pseudo-random behavior for replay tests.
Aisha Kapoor: Good catch — switched to a seeded Xoroshiro-based RNG utility and added tests to assert deterministic outputs for a given seed.
Priya Nair: The dev-collector example config includes an API key field; we should document that this is optional and show how to use a local stub receiver.
Aisha Kapoor: Documented the stub receiver and added a lightweight node-based stub in examples/simplay/telemetry/stub-receiver.js (dev-only).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash; changelog entry added to docs/quickstarts/simplay-quickstart.md and release notes prepared for internal release notes channel
notes_for_maintainers: Follow-up work suggested: (1) add an example showing how to wire simplay telemetry into Redwood Console staging pipelines; (2) add a small tutorial on using simplay to validate quantization and latency regressions by replaying generated sequences against different model configs; (3) consider moving dev-collector into a separate small service package if teams adopt it widely.
testing_steps: To validate locally: 1) git checkout feature/simplay-telemetry-shims 2) yarn install 3) yarn workspace @redwood/examples simplay:dev 4) open the sandbox at http://localhost:3000 or run simplay:cli run --seed 10 --scenario basic 5) inspect replay.json and telemetry.log 6) run yarn test tests/simplay to ensure unit/integration tests pass
